subagent_reports.topic: Best-practice patterns for a durable in-repo backlog shell store (.adv/backlog): storage format, Temporal-vs-filesystem authority, schema durability, lifecycle state machine, cross-worktree concurrency, Epic-shell complement vs replace

sources.label: Ctxo ADR-001 — single-JSON vs per-file storage decision
sources.summary: Formal ADR: single monolithic JSON = merge conflicts, large diffs, full rewrite every update, cannot parallelize writes; per-file JSON = conflicts scoped to changed item, small diffs, concurrent writes. Rejects committing SQLite (binary conflicts). Q1.

sources.label: Threlmark 'Disk Is the Contract' local-first architecture
sources.summary: temp-file + rename() atomic write; one-file-per-item to avoid races; read-merge-write preserving id/createdAt and unknown fields => forward-compatible; small index self-heals by reconciling items actually present. Q1, Q3, Q5.

sources.label: JSONLT — JSON Lines Table (append-only, last-entry-wins, git auto-merge)
sources.summary: Append-only JSON Lines keyed per record; updates append a new line (last entry per key wins). Two devs editing different records both append to different lines => git auto-merges, single-line diffs, grep/editor friendly. Matches ADV agenda.jsonl. Q1, Q5.

sources.label: 'Git as Database: Lessons from the Trenches'
sources.summary: Empirical: concurrent writers to one agents.json produce merge conflicts/garbage; fix was structural (one-file-per-entity OR append-only inbox+single applier) plus flock+retry (reinvented OCC). Single-file JSON has no query language; every read deserializes the whole file. Q1, Q5.

sources.label: sirdb — git-diffable JSON DB (1 file per record, single-node-thread ACID)
sources.summary: Per-record JSON files in per-table subdirs; human-readable, git-diffable, ACID as long as accessed by a single node thread (expand via request queue). Confirms per-item-file approach + single-writer ACID boundary. Q1, Q5.

sources.label: Temporal docs — Workflow Execution is source of truth; durability/recoverability
sources.summary: Event History is the definitive source of truth for workflow state; Durability = no imposed time limit; Reliability = fully recoverable, state persists/resumes. Temporal authoritative for workflow-scoped state but requires running worker + reachable service to read. Q2.

sources.label: Temporal docs — history size limit + continue-as-new
sources.summary: Temporal enforces a per-Event history size limit; unbounded state accumulation in one workflow requires continue-as-new. An ever-growing backlog is a poor fit for a single workflow's history; argues against Temporal owning an unbounded candidate pool. Q2.

sources.label: Linear workflow states + categories + Triage
sources.summary: Canonical opinionated backlog lifecycle: Backlog>Todo>In Progress>In Review>Done>Canceled across four categories (Unstarted, Started, Completed, Cancelled), optional Triage checkpoint gating entry to active backlog. Reference model for Q4.

sources.label: GuideMode status/state mapping
sources.summary: Cross-tool normalization: backlog (not prioritized) and ready (prioritized) both open/not-WIP; done and canceled both closed. Explicit backlog->ready->delivery transitions. Maps ADV draft/ready/archived onto industry-standard grouping. Q4.

sources.label: Jujutsu (jj) concurrency — lock-free operation log vs DVCS lock files
sources.summary: jj rejects lock files; accepts concurrent changes always happen and exposes conflicts (operation log detects/merges divergent ops; each op sees a consistent view and is guaranteed to commit). Pattern: let the VCS reconcile at item granularity rather than serialize with a global lock. Q5.

sources.label: Zod schema versioning/evolution (discriminatedUnion + migrate-on-read + passthrough)
sources.summary: Canonical Zod strategy: version-discriminated union of per-version schemas + version detector dispatching to the right parser + migration functions. Complemented by verzod (github.com/AndrewBastin/verzod) and zod-migrations (z.preprocess(migrate, schema.passthrough())) pairing migrate-on-read with passthrough to preserve unknown keys. Q3.

sources.label: ADV repo — atomicWriteFile + acquireFileLock (utils/fs.ts)
sources.summary: ADV already ships atomicWriteFile (mkdir -p, write tmp, handle.sync() flush, rename — POSIX-atomic, avoids NUL-truncation) and acquireFileLock (.lock w/ pid+timestamp, 30s stale reclaim gated on process.kill(pid,0) liveness, jittered backoff). Exact primitives Q1/Q3/Q5 recommend already exist, reusable.

sources.label: ADV repo — jsonl-atomic-writer.ts + agenda.ts atomic JSONL
sources.summary: writeJsonlAtomic serializes entries to newline-delimited JSON with tmp+rename (torn-write-safe); agenda.ts already uses atomic JSONL. In-repo precedent for the append-friendly, git-auto-mergeable JSONL shape recommended for the backlog.

sources.label: ADV repo — worker-lock.ts dual-schema migrate-on-read
sources.summary: readLockContents branches on parsed.schema_version === 2 and otherwise returns a v1 shape — canonical ADV migrate-on-read with explicit top-level version field. Direct in-repo precedent for the Q3 recommendation.

sources.label: ADV repo — pervasive Zod .passthrough() convention + git-tracked github-project.json
sources.summary: Every ADV domain schema terminates in .passthrough() 'Allow extra fields for forward/backward compatibility' (types/agenda.ts, types/project.ts, types/specs.ts). Lazy migrate-on-read (github-project-config.ts:12 'migrates forward on first read'; signals.ts:363 source:'migrate'). github-project.json is a git-tracked in-repo JSON config precedent. Q2, Q3.

sources.label: ADV spec — advance-epics rq-epicEntries01 (shells are Epic-parented, 1 of 2 entry kinds)
sources.summary: 'An Epic's ordered entries MUST support exactly two kinds: change entries ... and shell entries that represent future work.' Shells today MUST be Epic-parented, MUST have title+success hint; a change entry MAY carry promotion provenance when originated from a shell. Confirms the gap the backlog fills (un-parented shells) + the promotion-provenance pattern to mirror. Q6.

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: Q1 (storage format): Three external sources (Ctxo ADR-001, JSONLT, 'Git as Database') plus two reference impls (sirdb, Threlmark) converge — a SINGLE JSON ARRAY is the worst option for a multi-worktree git-tracked store: array edits touch multiple lines (trailing-comma churn), concurrent adds collide, reads deserialize the whole file, no query index. Conflict-free options: (a) append-only JSON Lines with last-entry-per-key-wins (git auto-merges disjoint appends; identical to ADV agenda.jsonl + jsonl-atomic-writer.ts) and (b) one-file-per-item under .adv/backlog/<id>.json + optional self-healing index. Since ADV already ships atomicWriteFile + writeJsonlAtomic + an agenda JSONL precedent, append-only JSONL (.adv/backlog.jsonl) is the lowest-novelty best-merge choice; per-item files are the scalable alternative for large bodies/per-item history. A single .adv/backlog.json array (as literally named) should be rejected. Q2 (Temporal vs filesystem): Temporal docs confirm Event History is the source of truth for workflow-scoped state and is durable/recoverable, but reading it needs a reachable service + running worker, and the per-Event history-size limit makes an unbounded long-lived candidate pool a poor payload (continue-as-new is overkill for a backlog). The backlog's needs invert Temporal's sweet spot: git-tracked, branch-local, greppable, readable with NO worker (fresh worktree or CI). Filesystem-authoritative is correct for the new tier. Do NOT migrate in-progress Epic shells out of Temporal; keep Temporal authoritative for Epic-bound entries, make the in-repo backlog a separate filesystem-authoritative candidate pool. Q3 (schema durability): Zod ecosystem (studyraid, verzod, zod-migrate, zod-migrations) and ADV's own conventions agree: top-level schemaVersion + migrate-on-read + terminal .passthrough(). ADV already does exactly this (worker-lock.ts dual-version read; universal .passthrough(); github-project.json migrated-forward-on-first-read). Backlog should carry a top-level schemaVersion integer, parse each item with a passthrough schema, migrate-on-read, refuse writes that would drop unknown fields (already in the proposal error table). Q4 (lifecycle): Linear/Jira/GitHub/Notion normalize to four categories — Unstarted, Started, Completed, Cancelled (GuideMode open/in_progress/closed). ADV's draft/ready/archived is a valid minimal machine: draft=Unstarted-unprioritized, ready=Unstarted-prioritized (Linear Todo), archived=terminal. Because a backlog item's Started/Completed phase is owned by the change/Epic it promotes into, the backlog needs NO in-progress state; it needs terminal states + a promotion edge. Recommend draft -> ready -> {promoted(change|epic) | archived}, archived as soft-delete (status flip retained in file, not hard-delete) so git history + provenance survive; promotion auto-flips to a terminal 'promoted' status carrying the target ref (mirrors rq-epicEntries01). Q5 (cross-worktree concurrency): jj's lock-free operation-log model teaches the durable lesson — for VCS-tracked shared state let the VCS reconcile at item granularity rather than impose a global lock. Item-granular storage (JSONL append or per-item files) reduces cross-worktree contention to git's own 3-way merge, near-conflict-free for disjoint items. ADV's acquireFileLock is right for intra-machine races (two tool calls in one checkout) but is NOT a cross-worktree/cross-commit authority — git is. Recommend item-granular shape + atomicWriteFile for local torn-write safety + acquireFileLock for same-checkout serialization; document that cross-worktree divergence resolves at git merge time; add per-item id + created_at + monotonic updated_at so stale writes are detectable (last-write-wins with provenance). CRDT is unjustified complexity at this scale (rejected). Q6 (complement vs replace): Every parallel system keeps a bounded-lifecycle container (Linear project/cycle, Jira epic, GitHub Projects, GitLab epic) SEPARATE from an unbounded product backlog, moving items between them by linking/promotion, not by relocating storage. The backlog is the unbounded candidate pool; Epics are bounded initiatives (active->completed->closed). The proposal's design — keep Epic-bound shells in Temporal, add a filesystem backlog as the un-parented pool, import via adv_epic_add_shell backlog_ref (one-way) / promote to change — is the industry-standard complement pattern. COMPLEMENT, do not replace. Bounded<->unbounded migration should be a linking/provenance operation, never a storage move that risks losing the Temporal-authoritative Epic entry.

validation.notes: Core architecture (filesystem-authoritative in-repo backlog as a separate tier; complement not replace Temporal Epic shells; schemaVersion + passthrough + migrate-on-read; idempotent promotion with provenance; git-level conflict resolution) is validated by 2+ external sources per question AND matches strong existing ADV in-repo precedents. ONE correction, not a blocker: the literal storage shape named in the proposal — a single '.adv/backlog.json' array — has the worst multi-worktree merge profile of all options and is contradicted by every Q1 source. Recommend item-granular storage: append-only '.adv/backlog.jsonl' (preferred; reuses agenda.jsonl + jsonl-atomic-writer.ts, best git auto-merge) OR per-item '.adv/backlog/<id>.json' + index (more scalable). Format substitution within the already-approved approach, resolvable in design; the proposal's own note 'auto-merge of large JSON arrays is hostile' already anticipates it.

tradeoffs: Append-only JSONL gives near-zero git merge conflicts and reuses ADV's agenda.jsonl/jsonl-atomic-writer.ts precedent, but grows unbounded (needs periodic compaction, which agenda.ts already models) and needs last-entry-per-key dedupe on read.

Per-item files (.adv/backlog/<id>.json) scale better for large item bodies and give per-item git history + smallest diffs, but add a directory of many small files and need a self-healing index for fast listing (Threlmark/sirdb).

A single .adv/backlog.json array is simplest to implement/read (one JSON.parse) but has the hostile merge profile every Q1 source warns against; that simplicity buys a recurring merge-conflict tax under multi-worktree use.

Filesystem-authoritative backlog is durable/git-tracked/worker-independent but loses Temporal's structured query, Visibility search attributes, and signal-driven consistency — acceptable because the backlog is a low-frequency candidate pool, not active workflow state.

schemaVersion + migrate-on-read + passthrough maximizes forward/backward compat and matches ADV convention, at the cost of maintaining migration functions and refusing lossy writes (already in the proposal error table).

Complement (keep Epic shells in Temporal) avoids a risky migration of in-progress Epic state, at the cost of two shell representations (Temporal Epic shell vs filesystem backlog item) that must share a promotion/provenance vocabulary to avoid drift.

alternatives_considered.rationale: Worst multi-worktree merge profile per Ctxo ADR-001, JSONLT, and 'Git as Database'; array line-churn + guaranteed concurrent-add conflicts + whole-file reads. Contradicted by every Q1 source and the proposal's own 'auto-merge of large JSON arrays is hostile' note.

Best git auto-merge for disjoint edits (JSONLT), reuses ADV's proven agenda.jsonl + writeJsonlAtomic precedent, grep/editor friendly, torn-write-safe. Compaction is solved in agenda.ts. Lowest novelty, highest fit.

Scales best, per-item git history, smallest diffs, independent concurrent writes (sirdb, Threlmark). More machinery (many files + index reconciliation). Fallback/upgrade path if JSONL line-length or per-item history becomes limiting.

alternatives_considered.option: All-Temporal (store backlog as workflow state like Epic shells today)
alternatives_considered.rationale: Not git-tracked/branch-local, unreadable without a reachable worker, and an unbounded candidate pool fights Temporal's per-Event history-size limit (needs continue-as-new). Inverts the backlog's core requirements.

Could add Temporal Visibility indexing over a filesystem-authoritative backlog for fast cross-change queries, but adds a sync/drift surface with no v1 payoff at candidate-pool scale. Revisit only if cross-project or high-volume querying is needed (both out of scope).

jj's lock-free lesson: a global lock does not span worktrees/commits (git does) and serializes unrelated edits. Use acquireFileLock only for same-checkout races; let git's 3-way merge reconcile cross-worktree divergence at item granularity.
Massive complexity for a low-frequency human-scale candidate pool. Item-granular storage + git merge + monotonic updated_at provenance covers realistic conflicts (P19 simplicity).

alternatives_considered.option: Replace Epic shells with the backlog (migrate in-progress Epic shells to filesystem)
alternatives_considered.rationale: Every parallel system (Linear, Jira, GitHub, GitLab) keeps bounded initiative containers separate from the unbounded backlog and links/promotes between them. Migrating in-progress Epic (Temporal-authoritative) state to files risks losing workflow guarantees. Complement via backlog_ref import + promotion provenance instead.

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Adopt the proposal's tier/complement architecture as validated, with ONE substitution: change the store from a single .adv/backlog.json array to item-granular storage — append-only .adv/backlog.jsonl (preferred, reuses agenda.jsonl + jsonl-atomic-writer.ts) or per-item .adv/backlog/<id>.json + index (fallback). Reuse utils/fs.ts atomicWriteFile for torn-write safety and acquireFileLock for same-checkout serialization; rely on git's 3-way merge (not a global lock) for cross-worktree reconciliation, with per-item id/created_at/monotonic updated_at provenance for last-write-wins detection. Persist a top-level schemaVersion, parse items through .passthrough() schemas, migrate-on-read, refuse lossy writes (matches worker-lock.ts + universal ADV convention). Use a minimal draft -> ready -> {promoted(change|epic) | archived} lifecycle with archived as soft-delete; the backlog needs no in-progress state because Started/Completed is owned by the promoted change/Epic. subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: The design is directionally sound and appropriately boring: append-only JSONL + git disjoint-line auto-merge + same-checkout advisory lock + soft-delete retention + idempotent (itemId,changeId) promotion + one-way Epic binding is a coherent local-first model mapping cleanly onto the 29-item contract (all 14 AC addressed, all 7 constraints and 8 avoidances respected at the shape level; complement-not-replace and no-CRDT/no-global-lock/no-single-array explicitly honored). However, the design's cited reuse primitives are factually wrong in ways that would mislead implementation and, if implemented literally, break the append-only contract: (1) it names writeJsonlAtomic as the append mechanism, but that primitive is a FULL-FILE tmp+rename rewrite whose own docstring says it is single-writer derived-export tooling with no cross-process locking; a full-file rewrite violates C1 (append-only, never rewrite whole file) and undermines AC10 (git 3-way merge of disjoint lines) since rename churns the entire blob. The correct precedent is agenda.ts's appendFile+acquireFileLock. (2) The .passthrough() precedent cited (worker-lock.ts) uses hand-rolled version branching, not Zod/.passthrough(). (3) The acquireFileLock 'flock' description is inverted (it is advisory .lock-sidecar). These are correctable naming/precedent inaccuracies, not a fundamental architecture flaw; the intended behavior (appendFile under lock, git merge=union, Zod schemas that ignore-unknown) is achievable and correct. Secondary hardening gaps: no .gitattributes merge=union strategy for the JSONL to make disjoint-line auto-merge robust (AC10 fragile without it); embedded-newline safety relies on JSON.stringify escaping (fine but unstated); malformed-line and last-writer-wins reduction across item/promotion/archive kinds are described but the reduction/ordering rule is not fully specified.

# Proposal: Add durable in-repo backlog for shell items

## Problem

Today there is no durable, in-repo place to park future work that is not yet ready for an Epic or change:
- **Agenda** (Temporal): quick items, worktree-scoped, not durable across worktree lifetimes
- **Epic shell entries** (Temporal): must live inside an Epic; standalone shells are not supported (per `.adv/specs/advance-epics/spec.json` line 38: "An Epic's ordered entries MUST support exactly two kinds: change entries … and shell entries")
- **ROADMAP.md** (durable in-repo, generated): mirror of GH Project, not a writable backlog
- **ADV change** (Temporal): active work, not future work

We need a new tier: standalone durable shell items, in-repo, promotable to either a change or an Epic entry. Specs are in-repo and durable (`git`-tracked, branch-local); future-work shells should be too.

## Approach (revised after discovery research)

Add `.adv/backlog.jsonl` (append-only JSONL, **NOT single JSON array**) as the new shell store. Items have:
- `id`, `title`, `description` / `success_hint`, `tags`, `created_at`, `status` (`draft` / `ready` / `archived`), `origin`

Persistence semantics:
- **Append-only JSONL** — each item is one line; new items appended; promotions append a final provenance line. Git auto-merges disjoint appends across worktrees. Single-array format rejected (whole-line churn, guaranteed concurrent-add conflicts).
- **Filesystem-authoritative**. No Temporal mirror. Backlog is git-tracked, branch-local, worker-independent.
- **Schema versioning**: top-level `schemaVersion: 1` per-file header + `migrate-on-read` + `.passthrough()` (mirrors existing `plugin/src/storage/worker-lock.ts:140-179` and `github-project.json` patterns).
- **Lifecycle**: `draft → ready → {promoted | archived}`. No in-progress state (started/completed owned by the promoted change/Epic). Archived = soft-delete — line marked but retained for audit.

New MCP tools (item-granular):
- `adv_backlog_add` — append a new shell item
- `adv_backlog_list` — stream + filter (status, tags, origin) by reading JSONL
- `adv_backlog_show` — read single item
- `adv_backlog_promote` — append a promotion-provenance line; replace shell row in any Epic that imported it; idempotent on the (item_id, change_id) pair
- `adv_backlog_archive` — append a soft-delete line (audit-retained)

Epic integration: `adv_epic_add_shell` accepts `backlog_ref` to import a backlog item as an Epic entry (one-way; the item is now Epic-bound). **Epic shells continue to live in Temporal** (`rq-epicEntries01`) — backlog is the unbounded candidate pool, not a replacement. COMPLEMENT, not replace.

Same-checkout concurrency: reuse `acquireFileLock` (`plugin/src/utils/fs.ts`). Cross-worktree concurrency: git 3-way merge at JSONL granularity (no global lock; lock-free jj lesson).

Spec: new `.adv/specs/backlog/spec.json` (parallel to `.adv/specs/advance-epics/spec.json`).

## Reused primitives (repo precedent)

| Primitive | Location | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `atomicWriteFile` / `acquireFileLock` | `plugin/src/utils/fs.ts:31-148` | Race-free item append; same-checkout safety |
| `writeJsonlAtomic` | `plugin/src/utils/jsonl-atomic-writer.ts` | JSONL append with atomicity |
| `migrate-on-read` + `.passthrough()` | `plugin/src/storage/worker-lock.ts:140-179`, `github-project.json` | Schema evolution without breaking old entries |
| JSONL precedent | `agenda.jsonl` | Stream-and-filter pattern |

## Research questions (resolved)

1. **Format** — append-only JSONL (preferred) vs per-item files (deferred). Single JSON array rejected.
2. **Temporal vs filesystem** — filesystem-authoritative. Temporal owns only Epic shells (`rq-epicEntries01`).
3. **Schema durability** — `schemaVersion` + migrate-on-read + `.passthrough()`.
4. **Lifecycle** — `draft → ready → {promoted | archived}`. No in-progress.
5. **Cross-worktree concurrency** — git 3-way merge owns cross-worktree. `acquireFileLock` only for same-checkout. No global lock, no CRDT.
6. **Complement vs replace** — COMPLEMENT. Keep Temporal Epic shells. Import via `backlog_ref`.

## Scope

**New files:**
- `.adv/specs/backlog/spec.json` — capability contract for `backlog` (parallel to `advance-epics`)
- `plugin/src/tools/backlog-shell.ts` — new MCP tool surface (`adv_backlog_add`, `adv_backlog_list`, `adv_backlog_show`, `adv_backlog_promote`, `adv_backlog_archive`)
- `.opencode/command/adv-backlog.md` (optional) — guided user flow for backlog CRUD (mirrors `/adv-epic` style)
- `.adv/backlog.jsonl` — durable in-repo shell store (git-tracked, branch-local, schema-versioned)

**Files modified:**
- `plugin/src/tools/epic.ts` — `adv_epic_add_shell` accepts `backlog_ref` (optional; degrades to inline title/hint when absent)
- `.adv/specs/advance-epics/spec.json` — Epic shell entry MAY reference a backlog item by `backlog_ref`; provenance preserved on promotion
- `plugin/src/tools/index.ts` + `tool-registry.ts` — register new tools
- `plugin/schemas/` — new Zod schemas for `backlog.jsonl` entries (regenerated via `pnpm run schemas:generate`)

**Spec deltas:**
- New capability: `.adv/specs/backlog/spec.json` with requirements for shell durability, JSONL schema versioning, lifecycle states, promotion idempotency, cross-worktree merge semantics
- `.adv/specs/advance-epics/spec.json` amendment: Epic shell entry kind may carry `backlog_ref`; the item is then Epic-bound; no standalone-mode round-trip

## Error handling

| Failure | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `.adv/backlog.jsonl` parse failure on read | Tool returns typed error with line/column; do not silently default to empty |
| `schemaVersion` mismatch on read | Reads old-version items (forward compat via migrate-on-read); refuses writes that would lose information |
| Promotion references missing change | Refuses; surfaces "create change first, then promote" path |
| Promotion retried after success | Returns already-linked change without creating duplicate row (idempotent on `(item_id, change_id)`) |
| `adv_epic_add_shell` with `backlog_ref` to archived item | Refuses; surfaces "item is archived, un-archive or use a different item" path |
| Concurrent appends from same checkout | `acquireFileLock` serializes; failed append leaves JSONL unchanged |
| File append fails mid-flight | `writeJsonlAtomic` rolls back; no partial line |
| Tool called before `.adv/backlog.jsonl` exists | Tool creates the file with `schemaVersion: 1` header + empty body on first add; refuses promote/archive against empty store |

## Success criteria

- `.adv/backlog.jsonl` is the new durable store for un-parented future work
- `adv_backlog_add` / `adv_backlog_list` / `adv_backlog_promote` / `adv_backlog_archive` all work
- Promotion to change is idempotent (retrying returns the already-linked change without duplicate rows)
- Backlog items importable into Epics via `adv_epic_add_shell` with `backlog_ref`
- New spec `.adv/specs/backlog/spec.json` is the contract
- Cross-worktree concurrent add works without merge conflicts (git auto-merge of disjoint JSONL appends)
- `acquireFileLock` serialization verified for same-checkout concurrency
- `migrate-on-read` + `.passthrough()` tested with at least one synthetic schemaVersion bump
- No regression: pre-push `pnpm run check` green, full test suite green

## Out of scope

- Migrating existing agenda items into backlog
- Cross-project backlog sharing
- GH Project / `ROADMAP.md` integration (deferred)
- Replacing Temporal storage of Epic-bound shells (research-confirmed: COMPLEMENT not replace)

# Design: Add durable in-repo backlog for shell items

## Architecture

`.adv/backlog.jsonl` is a new append-only JSONL file in `.adv/`. Holds **standalone durable shell items** — future work not yet ready for an Epic or change. Items can be promoted to ADV changes or imported into Epics as bound shell entries.

### Storage model — append-only JSONL with advisory lock

**Real append precedent:** `appendFile(...)+"\n"` under `acquireFileLock`. Mirrors `plugin/src/storage/agenda.ts:279-286`.

**NOT `writeJsonlAtomic`:** that helper does full-file rewrite in memory + tmp+rename (see `plugin/src/storage/jsonl-atomic-writer.ts:29-51`). It's scoped to single-writer derived Temporal exports. For per-item append in a multi-read file, `appendFile` is the right primitive.

**Lock semantics:** `acquireFileLock` (`plugin/src/utils/fs.ts:73-148`) is an **advisory `.lock` sidecar** with PID + timestamp staleness check. Same-checkout serialization only. Cross-worktree correctness relies on git 3-way merge of disjoint appends (see Cross-worktree merge section).

**Why JSONL (not single JSON array):**
- Concurrent appends from different worktrees are disjoint lines → git auto-merges without conflict (with `.gitattributes` `merge=union`).
- Per-line schema (each entry is a self-contained object).
- Stream-parse-friendly (`readline` for large files).

**Why not per-item files (deferred):**
- More I/O (small file per item); more filesystem noise in `.adv/`. Reified file-per-item + index JSON deferred — only worth it at >100s of items.

### File format

```jsonl
{"kind":"header","schemaVersion":1,"createdAt":"2026-07-07T00:00:00Z"}
{"kind":"item","id":"bl-Hf7dK2mN","title":"Refactor X","description":"...","tags":["refactor","urgent"],"createdAt":"2026-07-07T00:00:00Z","status":"draft","origin":{"kind":"user","source":"session"}}
{"kind":"item","id":"bl-Abc123Xy","title":"Add Y","description":"...","tags":["feature"],"createdAt":"2026-07-07T00:00:01Z","status":"ready","origin":{"kind":"discovery","source":"task-tk-xyz"}}
{"kind":"promotion","itemId":"bl-Abc123Xy","changeId":"myChange","promotedAt":"2026-07-07T00:01:00Z","promotedBy":"agent"}
{"kind":"archive","itemId":"bl-Hf7dK2mN","archivedAt":"2026-07-07T00:02:00Z","reason":"superseded"}
```

**Line kinds:** `header` (file start), `item`, `promotion` (provenance for change promotion), `archive` (soft-delete marker).

**Idempotency:** `adv_backlog_promote` writes a `promotion` line. Re-running checks for an existing `promotion` line with the same `(itemId, changeId)` pair → returns the existing change without writing a duplicate.

## Schema versioning

- Top-level `schemaVersion: 1` in `header` line.
- All Zod schemas use `.passthrough()` to allow unknown fields for forward-compat.
- For migrate-on-read patterns, see `plugin/src/temporal/worker-lock.ts:140-179` (hand-rolled branching per version — NOT Zod passthrough; cited here for the migrate-function shape, not the field-tolerance mechanism).
- Migrate functions in `plugin/src/utils/backlog-migrations.ts`.

## Tool surface (5 new MCP tools)

`plugin/src/tools/backlog-shell.ts`:

| Tool | Args | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `adv_backlog_add` | `title`, `description`, `tags?`, `origin?` | `{itemId, createdAt}` |
| `adv_backlog_list` | `status?`, `tags?`, `limit?`, `offset?` | `{items: [...], total}` |
| `adv_backlog_show` | `itemId` | `{item, promotions, archives}` |
| `adv_backlog_promote` | `itemId`, `changeId` | `{promoted: boolean, changeId}` (idempotent) |
| `adv_backlog_archive` | `itemId`, `reason?` | `{archived: boolean, archivedAt}` |

All tools:
- Read: stream JSONL via `readline`; filter in memory.
- Write: `acquireFileLock` → `appendFile(content+"\n")` → release lock. All wrapped in `plugin/src/utils/backlog-store.ts`.

**Read-time reduction:** if file size > 1MB, `adv_backlog_list` reads only the last N lines (default 1000) by tail-seek; older items require explicit `offset`/`limit` pagination. Reduces TTI for large backlogs.

## Epic integration

`adv_epic_add_shell` (in `plugin/src/tools/epic.ts`) gains optional `backlog_ref`:

**Current signature** (`plugin/src/tools/epic.ts:1214-1271`): flat positional `{epic_id, title (required), success_hint (required), order?}`.

**New signature:**
- Args: `epic_id`, `title?`, `success_hint?`, `order?`, `backlog_ref?`
- **When `backlog_ref` is present:** `title` and `success_hint` become OPTIONAL — derived from backlog item if not provided.
- **When `backlog_ref` is absent:** `title` and `success_hint` are REQUIRED (existing contract preserved).
- Backward compat: existing call patterns continue to work.

Provenance: imported shell carries `imported_from: { backlog_id, imported_at }`. Bound one-way — cannot round-trip back to standalone. The backlog line stays in JSONL for audit; the Epic shell entry is the active reference.

## Cross-worktree merge

Add `.adv/backlog.jsonl merge=union` to `.gitattributes` so git auto-merges disjoint appends across worktrees.

- Two worktrees append disjoint lines → git 3-way merge succeeds.
- Two worktrees append lines for the same item → conflict; manual resolution (rare; coordinate via Epic promotion).

## Spec contract

New `.adv/specs/backlog/spec.json` (8 initial requirements):
- `rq-backlogDurability01` — git-tracked, branch-local
- `rq-backlogFormat01` — JSONL with `schemaVersion` header; never single-array
- `rq-backlogLifecycle01` — states `draft`, `ready`, `archived`; no in-progress
- `rq-backlogPromotion01` — idempotent on `(itemId, changeId)`
- `rq-backlogArchive01` — soft-delete (line marked, retained)
- `rq-backlogSchemaVersion01` — `schemaVersion` + migrate-on-read + `.passthrough()`
- `rq-backlogConcurrency01` — same-checkout via `acquireFileLock`; cross-worktree via git 3-way merge
- `rq-backlogEpicBridge01` — `adv_epic_add_shell` accepts `backlog_ref`; one-way bound

**Capability purpose:** "A durable in-repo store for future work items that are not yet ready for an active Epic or change. Items are JSONL-encoded, git-tracked, branch-local, and promotable to either an ADV change or an Epic shell entry."

## Implementation strategy

**New files:**
- `plugin/src/tools/backlog-shell.ts` — MCP tool definitions
- `plugin/src/utils/backlog-store.ts` — read/write primitives (`appendFile + acquireFileLock` + `readline` stream parse)
- `plugin/src/utils/backlog-migrations.ts` — schema version migrations
- `.adv/specs/backlog/spec.json` — capability contract
- `.opencode/command/adv-backlog.md` — guided user flow (mirrors `/adv-epic` style)
- Tests: `backlog-shell.test.ts`, `backlog-store.test.ts`, `backlog-migrations.test.ts`, `backlog-concurrency.test.ts`

**Modified files:**
- `plugin/src/tools/epic.ts` — `adv_epic_add_shell` signature: `title`/`success_hint` become optional when `backlog_ref` present; required when absent
- `.adv/specs/advance-epics/spec.json` — amendment for `backlog_ref`
- `plugin/src/tools/index.ts` + `plugin/src/tool-registry.ts` — register
- `plugin/src/schema-registry.ts` — add Zod
- `plugin/schemas/` — regenerated via `pnpm run schemas:generate`
- `.gitattributes` — add `merge=union` for `.adv/backlog.jsonl`

## Test strategy

- **Unit:** each `adv_backlog_*` tool against in-memory JSONL store
- **Concurrency:** two simultaneous appends (same-checkout); second waits on lock; verify line order preserved
- **Cross-worktree merge:** simulate with `git merge` of two branches each with disjoint appends + `.gitattributes` `merge=union`
- **Schema migration:** synthetic `schemaVersion: 0` file → migrate to current → verify
- **Promotion idempotency:** call twice → second returns existing; no duplicate line
- **Epic bridge:** with `backlog_ref` provided → import; without → existing behavior; verify `title`/`success_hint` derivation
- **Edge cases:** archived item import attempt → refused; malformed JSONL → typed error with line/column; file size > 1MB → read-time reduction kicks in (tail-read with pagination)

## Architectural risks

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Same-item concurrent edits from sibling worktrees | Rare; documented as manual-conflict scenario in spec |
| Schema migration data loss | `migrate-on-read` is non-destructive; refuses writes against old schema without explicit consent |
| Backlog line growth unbounded | Optional compaction (deferred); read-time reduction for >1MB files |
| `acquireFileLock` portability | Advisory sidecar only; cross-process safety relies on git merge + same-process serialization |
| `adv_epic_add_shell` backward compat | `backlog_ref` optional; existing required-arg patterns preserved when no `backlog_ref` |
| `appendFile` not atomic | Wrap in `acquireFileLock`; failure releases lock; partial line invalidates next-read (typed error with line/column) |
| `.gitattributes` not in repo | Documented as required operator step; pre-archive check |
